title: Add config history + preflight validator Helm flags, secrets, and env-specific toggles
author: Michael Nguyen
body:
Summary: This PR updates the redwood-helm-charts deployment to support the new Optimize config versioning components: (1) config-history service (version store API + apply/rollback control plane endpoints) and (2) preflight-validator service (safe-apply validation + dry-run/diff generation). It adds enablement flags, secret wiring, and environment-specific defaults so we can roll out internal -> Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private without chart forks.

Context: As part of Safe apply + rollback mechanism, we’re introducing new control-plane services that must be deployable alongside existing console/control-plane releases. SRE asked for explicit toggles per env, and Security Ops asked that all sensitive values be sourced from Kubernetes Secrets (or external secret providers) with least-privilege defaults.

Key changes: - New values toggles: optimize.configHistory.enabled (default false), optimize.preflightValidator.enabled (default false) and per-env overlays in values-hosted.yaml / values-dedicated.yaml / values-private.yaml. - New deployments/services: optimize-config-history and optimize-preflight-validator templates added (following existing control-plane chart conventions). - Secret management: support either (a) user-provided existingSecretName or (b) chart-managed Secret templates (disabled by default in prod overlays). The services require DB connection string (version store), encryption key reference (for at-rest envelope encryption), and internal service auth token/jwt key depending on installation mode. - External Secrets compatibility: the chart now cleanly references secret keys by name (no templated generation required) so Private customers can use their own secret provisioning (Vault/ESO/SealedSecrets). - RBAC/service accounts: added dedicated serviceAccounts with minimal RBAC for config-history and preflight-validator; both use existing control-plane network policy patterns. - Pod security + reliability knobs: resources defaults, PDBs, topologySpreadConstraints, and liveness/readiness probes added; HPA stubs included but disabled by default (SRE wants to tune after observing rollout). - Config propagation safety: added rollout-specific env vars/flags (OPTIMIZE_CONFIG_APPLY_LOCK_TTL_MS, OPTIMIZE_CONFIG_PROPAGATION_STATUS_ENABLED) and made them configurable via values for phased enablement.

Values/flags added (high level): - optimize.configHistory.enabled - optimize.configHistory.image.repository/tag - optimize.configHistory.service.port - optimize.configHistory.env (extraEnv) - optimize.configHistory.secrets.existingSecretName - optimize.configHistory.secrets.keys (dbUrl, signingKey, encryptionKeyRef) - optimize.configHistory.featureFlags.enableAuditEvents (default true in hosted/dedicated, configurable in private) - optimize.preflightValidator.enabled - optimize.preflightValidator.image.repository/tag - optimize.preflightValidator.secrets.existingSecretName - optimize.preflightValidator.guardrails.profile ("conservative" default) - optimize.preflightValidator.dryRunSimulation.enabled

Upgrade notes: - No behavior change unless enabled flags are set. - For internal/hosted rollouts, the platform team should provision secrets named optimize-config-history-secrets and optimize-preflight-validator-secrets in the target namespace, containing required keys documented in values.yaml comments. - For Private installs, the overlays default both services off; when enabled, the installer should ensure migrations/DB reachability are in place (see ENG-4821 / private installer work).

Testing: - helm lint + template render against hosted/dedicated/private overlays - kubeconform schema validation in CI - basic install test in staging (control-plane namespace) verified that templates render with both existingSecretName and chart-managed secret disabled

Checklist: - [x] Charts render with both services disabled (default) - [x] Charts render with configHistory enabled only - [x] Charts render with both services enabled + existingSecretName - [x] Probes/PDBs present and match SRE guidelines - [x] No secret values in ConfigMaps; all sensitive fields sourced from Secret keys - [x] Added docs in values.yaml comments for required secret keys

Notes for reviewers: Most of this PR is boilerplate chart wiring, but please pay attention to: (1) secret key naming consistency (so other repos can provision them reliably), (2) default enablement in env overlays, and (3) whether we should ship chart-managed Secret templates at all (currently present but off-by-default and not referenced by overlays).
commits: charts(redwood): add optimize-config-history and optimize-preflight-validator templates behind flags
charts(values): introduce env overlays for hosted/dedicated/private enablement defaults
security: wire secretKeyRef for db url + signing key + encryption key refs; remove plaintext placeholders
sre: add probes, pdb, resource defaults, and topology spread constraints for new services
ci: extend chart rendering matrix to include new flag combinations
review_conversation: Chloe Martin: Can we standardize the secret keys? Backend expects OPTIMIZE_VERSION_STORE_DB_URL and OPTIMIZE_INTERNAL_SIGNING_KEY; right now chart uses dbUrl/signingKey. Prefer using fixed keys in the Secret to avoid drift across installers.

Michael Nguyen (author): Good call. Updated to use secret keys: optimizeVersionStoreDbUrl, optimizeInternalSigningKey, optimizeEncryptionKeyRef (consistent with control-plane conventions). Also added explicit comments in values.yaml and updated templates accordingly.
Neha Kapoor: Please add a PDB and make sure readiness gates don’t flap during DB outages; readiness should fail if DB is unreachable but liveness should not hard-restart the pod in a tight loop.

Michael Nguyen (author): Added PDB (minAvailable: 1) and adjusted liveness to only check process health; readiness checks DB connectivity via /ready endpoint (service returns non-200 if DB unreachable).
Benji Okafor: For apply locking, we need the lock TTL exposed as a value. Also please ensure private overlay defaults conservative guardrails for validator.

Michael Nguyen (author): Added optimize.configHistory.applyLockTtlMs value (default 300000) and wired OPTIMIZE_CONFIG_APPLY_LOCK_TTL_MS. Private overlay sets validator.guardrails.profile=conservative and keeps service disabled by default.
Svetlana Petrenko: Any plans for audit export/SIEM webhook config here? At least ensure we can configure the audit sink endpoint without a chart edit.
Michael Nguyen (author): Added optimize.configHistory.audit.sinkUrl as an optional env var (non-secret) and audit.sinkAuthTokenSecretKeyRef for the token (secret). Both are unset by default.

Connor O'Brien: Release train ask: keep both services disabled in default values; only enable via env overlays and feature flags. Also add a note that chart-managed Secret templates should not be used in prod.
Michael Nguyen (author): Default values remain disabled. Added explicit comments: chart-managed Secret templates are for dev only; prod should use existingSecretName/external secret providers.
Connor O'Brien: Approved once the comments land and the render matrix includes both enablement combos.
Neha Kapoor: Approved after probe changes.
Chloe Martin: Approved after secret key naming fix.
release_notes: Helm charts now support deploying Optimize config history (versioning/apply/rollback control plane) and preflight validator services behind environment-specific flags, with Secret-based configuration and conservative private defaults.
